claim: Enhanced fan-out lets a consumer receive records from a stream with dedicated throughput of up to 2 MB of data per second per shard, so it does not contend with other consumers of the stream.
question: What read throughput does an enhanced fan-out consumer get, and does it share it with other consumers?

values.display: up to 2 MB of data per second per shard
throughput is dedicated

qualifiers.scope: per shard, per enhanced fan-out consumer

evidence.quote: This feature lets consumers receive records from a stream with throughput of up to 2 MB of data per second per shard. This throughput is dedicated, which means that consumers that use enhanced fan-out don't have to contend with other consumers that are receiving data from the stream.

claim: With enhanced fan-out, Kinesis Data Streams pushes data records from the stream to the consumers, so the consumers do not need to poll for data.
question: Does an enhanced fan-out consumer poll the stream, or does the stream push records to it?

values.display: pushes data records from the stream to consumers
don't need to poll for data

evidence.quote: Kinesis Data Streams pushes data records from the stream to consumers that use enhanced fan-out. Therefore, these consumers don't need to poll for data.

claim: Shared-throughput consumers share a fixed total of 2 MB/sec of read throughput per shard. With enhanced fan-out, each registered consumer receives its own read throughput per shard, up to 2 MB/sec, independently of other consumers.
question: How does read throughput per shard differ between shared-throughput consumers and enhanced fan-out consumers?

values.display: Fixed at a total of 2 MB/sec per shard
its own read throughput per shard, up to 2 MB/sec

evidence.quote: | Read throughput | Fixed at a total of 2 MB/sec per shard. If there are multiple consumers reading from the same shard, they all share this throughput. The sum of the throughputs they receive from the shard doesn't exceed 2 MB/sec. | Scales as consumers register to use enhanced fan-out. Each consumer registered to use enhanced fan-out receives its own read throughput per shard, up to 2 MB/sec, independently of other consumers. |
evidence.table_header: | Characteristics | Shared throughput consumers without enhanced fan-out | Enhanced fan-out consumers |

claim: Message propagation delay of a shared-throughput consumer averages around 200 ms with one consumer and around 1000 ms with five consumers. An enhanced fan-out consumer typically averages 70 ms with one consumer or five.
question: What is the typical message propagation delay of shared-throughput consumers compared with enhanced fan-out consumers?

values.display: around 200 ms
around 1000 ms
average of 70 ms

qualifiers.condition: shared-throughput consumers read with GetRecords; enhanced fan-out consumers read with SubscribeToShard

evidence.quote: | Message propagation delay | An average of around 200 ms if you have one consumer reading from the stream. This average goes up to around 1000 ms if you have five consumers. | Typically an average of 70 ms whether you have one consumer or five consumers. |
evidence.table_header: | Characteristics | Shared throughput consumers without enhanced fan-out | Enhanced fan-out consumers |

consumer-shard hour cost

claim: Shared-throughput consumers use a pull model over HTTP with GetRecords. Enhanced fan-out consumers get records pushed to them over HTTP/2 with SubscribeToShard.
question: Which API and protocol does each consumer type use to receive records?

values.display: Pull model over HTTP using GetRecords
pushes the records to you over HTTP/2 using SubscribeToShard

evidence.quote: | Record delivery model | Pull model over HTTP using GetRecords. | Kinesis Data Streams pushes the records to you over HTTP/2 using SubscribeToShard. |
evidence.table_header: | Characteristics | Shared throughput consumers without enhanced fan-out | Enhanced fan-out consumers |

claim: With KCL version 2.0 or later, the KCL sets up the consumer to use enhanced fan-out on all shards of the stream. If you build the consumer with the API, you can subscribe to individual shards.
question: How does a consumer built with KCL 2.0 or later use enhanced fan-out, compared with one built with the API?

values.display: all the shards of the stream
subscribe to individual shards

evidence.quote: If you use version 2.0 or later of the Amazon Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to build a consumer, the KCL sets up the consumer to use enhanced fan-out to receive data from all the shards of the stream. If you use the API to build a consumer that uses enhanced fan-out, then you can subscribe to individual shards.

claim: A consumer that uses enhanced fan-out gets its own 2 MB/sec allotment of read throughput. Several consumers can read the same stream in parallel without contending for read throughput with other consumers.
question: Why do several consumers of one stream use enhanced fan-out?

values.display: its own 2 MB/sec allotment of read throughput
read data from the same stream in parallel

evidence.quote: When a consumer uses *enhanced fan-out*, it gets its own 2 MB/sec allotment of read throughput, allowing multiple consumers to read data from the same stream in parallel, without contending for read throughput with other consumers.

claim: The Kinesis Client Library is a Java library that simplifies consuming data from Kinesis Data Streams. It manages load balancing across workers, responding to worker failures, checkpointing processed records, and responding to changes in the number of shards.
question: What does the Kinesis Client Library manage for a consumer application?

values.display: load balancing across multiple workers
checkpointing processed records

evidence.quote: Kinesis Client Library (KCL) is a standalone Java software library designed to simplify the process of consuming and processing data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. KCL handles many of the complex tasks associated with distributed computing, letting developers focus on implementing their business logic for processing data. It manages activities such as load balancing across multiple workers, responding to worker failures, checkpointing processed records, and responding to changes in the number of shards in the stream.

claim: The Kinesis Client Library provides built-in fault tolerance, so processing continues if individual workers fail, and it provides at-least-once delivery.
question: What delivery guarantee does the Kinesis Client Library provide?

values.display: at-least-once delivery
built-in fault tolerance mechanisms

evidence.quote: KCL provides built-in fault tolerance mechanisms, making sure that data processing continues even if individual workers fail. KCL also provides at-least-once delivery.
